standfirst: Some people started talking about a debt crisis in Japan. In this report, I discuss why Japan's net interest payments will remain the lowest among the Indebted Five: US, UK, France, Italy and Japan
_note: Titles, subtitles and source notes are the TITLE / SUBTITLE / SOURCE / YLABEL constants of each chart script in the JMA chart library, copied verbatim. Data cut from the library master CSVs by cut_data.py per the exhibit ledger in the report record (30.Reports/2026-08/2026-08-18-jgb-effective-rate-sub.md), which re-derives every figure the report prints and refuses to write on disagreement. The page carries the five published exhibits only (Takuji's ruling, 2026-08-12: a report page shows the report's charts). The slug follows the report's own date, 18 August; the masthead carries the publication date, 19 August. Germany is absent from charts 2 and 3, and Canada was never in the net-interest file at all -- that omission is why the claim reads 'Indebted Five' and not G7, and neither country may be restored without re-checking the claim.
_series_order: No two series share a history column on any exhibit here, so the shared-history colour trap does not arise. Chart 1 and Chart 3 carry one column per series plus a phase flag, split solid over the actuals and dotted over the projection. On Chart 4 the shaded band is listed before the two lines so they draw on top of it.

charts.subtitle: UK's is 13.4 years, but it issues sizable inflation indexed bonds
charts.source: Source: UK DMO, US Treasury (MSPD), Italy MEF, Agence France Trésor, JMA estimate for Japan's. Bonds plus bills; loans excluded. JGB includes FILP bonds and T-bills include FB.
charts.note: All five on one definition: gross marketable central-government securities, coupon bonds plus short-term bills, loans excluded. The UK is published quarterly, the others monthly; every line is drawn across its reporting gaps, as the published chart does.

charts.label: Chart 3
charts.title: Among the "Indebted Five", Japan pays the lowest interest
charts.subtitle: General government net interest paid, % of GDP; dashed = IMF projection
charts.source: Source: IMF WEO (Apr 2026), JMA. Net interest = interest expense minus interest revenue, general government.
charts.note: The WEO publishes no interest series; net interest is its overall balance minus its primary balance, computed by JMA.
